We need a retrosynthesis route with max 1 step (i.e., direct synthesis from commercially available chemicals). Leaves must be commercially available and total price <= $125. Need to propose a route using a template that matches our target. Template 38636 seems to be an ester formation: product is an ester formed from an acid (or acid derivative) and an alcohol. The retro template: product (ester) -> acid (O-[C]=O) + alcohol (C-OH). The retro_smarts: [C:6]-[O;H0;D2;+0:7]-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]-[C:4]=[C:5]>> O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[C:3]-[C:4]=[C:5] . [C:6]-[OH;D1;+0:7]

So product is an ester where the alkoxy part is C6-O- (the alcohol). The acid part is O-C(=O)-C3-C4=C5 (i.e., a carboxylic acid attached to a conjugated alkene aromatic system). Our target: COC( ... )=O is a methyl ester (methoxy). So the alcohol is methanol (CH3OH). The acid part is O=C(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)O? Wait the target is COC( ... )=O, i.e., methyl ester of a carboxylic acid: O=C( ... )OCH3. So the acid precursor would be the corresponding carboxylic acid: O=C(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)O (i.e., the same skeleton with OH instead of OCH3). So we need to see if that acid is commercially available. We checked is_buyable and got False. So not directly.

But we can consider other routes: maybe using acyl chloride + methanol. The template may also handle acyl chloride? Another template may involve formation of ester from acid chloride and alcohol. Let's search for templates where functional_groups_broken includes "acyl chloride" and formed "carboxylic esters". Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional_groups_broken = ["acyl chloride"], functional_groups_formed = ["carboxylic esters"].
